label: override_express
decision: Hubbard v. United States
title: False Statements Accountability Act of 1996
point: Held that 1001 ('any department or agency of the United States') does not reach false statements made in judicial proceedings.
change: Rewrote 1001 to cover matters within the jurisdiction of the 'executive, legislative, or judicial branch' of the Government.
why: The new words reach the judicial branch, reversing the decision's point, and the report says the bill responds to Hubbard.

label: override_express
decision: Bailey v. United States
point: Held that 'use' of a firearm under 924(c)(1) requires active employment, so mere proximity and accessibility of a gun to drugs is not enough.
change: Restructured 924(c)(1) and added liability for anyone who 'in furtherance of any such crime, possesses a firearm', plus tiered minimums.
why: The new possession-in-furtherance prong reaches the passive possession Bailey held outside 'use'; the committee report describes Bailey's active-employment holding as the reason for the change.

label: override_express
decision: Commissioner v. Lundy
title: Taxpayer Relief Act of 1997
point: Held that when a non-filer receives a notice of deficiency before filing a return, the 2-year look-back in 6512(b)(3)(B) applies, so the Tax Court cannot refund withheld taxes.
change: Added that when the notice is mailed in the third year after the due date and no return was filed, the look-back period is 3 years.
why: The new sentence gives taxpayers in Lundy's situation a 3-year look-back, reversing the result, and the report describes Lundy as the case addressed.

label: override_express
decision: United States v. Turner
point: Applying Bailey's 'active employment' reading of 'uses' in 924(c)(1) retroactively, the court vacated a conviction where the gun merely sat in a handbag with cocaine.
change: The Act restructured 924(c)(1) to also punish anyone who 'in furtherance of any such crime, possesses a firearm,' with graded minimums.
why: The committee report cites this decision among post-Bailey vacaturs it meant to address, and under the new possession-in-furtherance prong, a gun stored with drugs, as in Turner, can support a conviction.

label: override_express
decision: United States v. Hung Shun Lin
point: Reversed Lin's 924(c) convictions because the jury instruction on 'use' was foreclosed by Bailey's active-employment reading.
change: Added a separate offense for possessing a firearm 'in furtherance of' a crime of violence or drug crime, and restructured penalties into graded minimums.
why: The 1998 Act answered Bailey by reaching possession in furtherance, closing the gap that forced reversal in Lin; the committee report cites Lin as an example of convictions lost under Bailey.

label: override_express
decision: National Credit Union Administration v. First National Bank & Trust Co.
title: Credit Union Membership Access Act
point: Held that 1759's common-bond requirement unambiguously requires the same common bond to unite every member of an occupational credit union, invalidating NCUA's multiple-group interpretation.
change: Struck the common-bond clause and added 1759(b) expressly authorizing multiple common-bond credit unions, among other membership categories.
why: The new text allows the multiple-group credit unions the Court held unlawful, and the report says the Act responds to this Supreme Court decision.

label: override_express
decision: Bossier Parish School Board v. Reno
title: Fannie Lou Hamer, Rosa Parks, and Coretta Scott King Voting Rights Act Reauthorization and Amendments Act of 2006
point: On remand, granted preclearance, treating the section 5 purpose inquiry as limited to retrogressive intent (later affirmed in Bossier Parish II).
change: Added 1973c(c): purpose includes any discriminatory purpose.
why: The new subsection reverses the retrogressive-purpose limit applied here, and the Act names Bossier Parish II in the same litigation.

label: override_express
decision: Sutton v. United Air Lines, Inc.
title: ADA Amendments Act of 2008
point: Held that mitigating measures must be considered in deciding whether an impairment substantially limits a major life activity, relying on the ADA findings (including the 43 million figure) to read 'disability' narrowly.
change: The ADAAA rewrote the 12101 findings (dropping the 43 million and 'discrete and insular minority' findings) and redefined disability to exclude consideration of mitigating measures.
why: The Act's findings name Sutton as having narrowed the ADA's intended scope and the amendments reverse its mitigating-measures rule and the findings it relied on.

label: override_implicit
decision: United States v. Cisneros
title: Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004
point: Held that 'facility in interstate or foreign commerce' in 1958(a) requires actual interstate or foreign use of the facility in the particular instance, not the broad 'facility of interstate commerce' definition, though the conviction stood on international calls.
change: Changed 1958(a) to 'facility of interstate or foreign commerce' and conformed the definition, so intrastate use of such a facility suffices.
why: The amendment adopts the broad reading the court rejected, so its narrow interpretation no longer holds; nothing in the packet ties Congress to this case.

label: override_express
decision: Reno v. Bossier Parish School Board
title: Fannie Lou Hamer, Rosa Parks, and Coretta Scott King Voting Rights Act Reauthorization and Amendments Act of 2006
point: Held that the section 5 purpose prong reaches only retrogressive purpose, so a discriminatory but nonretrogressive plan must be precleared.
change: Added 1973c(c): purpose includes any discriminatory purpose.
why: The new subsection reverses the holding, and the Act's findings and report name Bossier Parish II.

label: override_implicit
decision: Food & Drug Administration v. Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp.
point: Held the FDA lacked authority under the FDCA to regulate tobacco products, reasoning in part that under 331(a) misbranded tobacco 'devices' would have to be removed from the market.
change: Inserted 'tobacco product' into 331(a)'s prohibited acts, as part of giving FDA express authority over tobacco products under a new chapter.
why: Congress gave FDA the jurisdiction over tobacco that the Court found missing, so the decision's conclusion no longer holds; the packet shows no passage naming the case.

label: override_express
decision: Immigration & Naturalization Service v. St. Cyr
title: Emergency Supplemental Appropriations Act for Defense, the Global War on Terror, and Tsunami Relief, 2005
point: The Court held that 1252(a)(1) and (a)(2)(C) speak only of 'judicial review' and do not clearly strip district courts of habeas jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. 2241 over criminal aliens' removal challenges.
change: The REAL ID Act inserted 'including section 2241 of title 28, or any other habeas corpus provision' into the jurisdiction-stripping provisions of 1252(a)(2) and added a petition for review as the exclusive means of review.
why: The new words supply exactly the clear statement St. Cyr found missing, eliminating 2241 habeas review, and the committee report names St. Cyr as the decision being answered.

label: override_implicit
decision: Lorillard Tobacco Co. v. Reilly
point: Held that FCLAA 1334(b) pre-empts Massachusetts' location-based restrictions on outdoor and point-of-sale cigarette advertising.
change: Amended 1334(a) to let FDA require different package warnings, and the same Act added 1334(c) letting States impose time, place and manner (not content) restrictions on cigarette advertising.
why: The new 1334(c) removes pre-emption for exactly the location restrictions Lorillard held pre-empted; the law names Lorillard only for First Amendment guidance on FDA rules, not as the reason for the pre-emption change.

label: override_express
decision: Toyota Motor Manufacturing, Kentucky, Inc. v. Williams
title: ADA Amendments Act of 2008
point: Read 'substantially limits' and 'major life activities' strictly, relying on the 43 million finding in 12101(a)(1), to create a demanding standard for disability.
change: Struck the 43 million finding, rewrote the disability definition and directed broad construction.
why: The ADAAA rejects the decision's demanding standard and its findings name this decision as having narrowed the ADA.

label: override_express
decision: Ashcroft v. Free Speech Coalition
title: Prosecutorial Remedies and Other Tools to end the Exploitation of Children Today Act of 2003" or "PROTECT Act
point: Held the CPPA's 'appears to be' a minor (2256(8)(B)) and 'conveys the impression' (2256(8)(D)) definitions overbroad under the First Amendment.
change: The PROTECT Act rewrote 2256(8) (computer-generated images 'indistinguishable from' real minors), replaced (D) with a pandering offence, and raised 2251 penalties.
why: The Act's findings and report identify Free Speech Coalition and the law rewrites the very definitions it struck down; the 2251 changes themselves are penalties.

label: override_express
decision: Holmes Group, Inc. v. Vornado Air Circulation Systems, Inc.
title: Leahy-Smith America Invents Act
point: Held a patent-law counterclaim does not make a case 'arise under' patent law for 1338(a), so the Federal Circuit lacked appellate jurisdiction under 1295(a)(1).
change: Replaced the state-court exclusivity sentence in 1338(a) with a bar on any State court jurisdiction over any claim for relief arising under patent, plant variety or copyright law (with related changes to 1295 for compulsory counterclaims).
why: The law makes patent counterclaims (any claim for relief) exclusively federal and, through the related 1295 change, gives the Federal Circuit the appeals Holmes denied; the report names Holmes as the decision addressed.

label: override_express
decision: Moseley v. V Secret Catalogue, Inc.
title: Trademark Dilution Revision Act of 2006
point: Held the FTDA requires proof of actual dilution, not likelihood of dilution, reinforcing that reading with the 1127 definition of dilution as an actual 'lessening of the capacity' of a mark.
change: Struck the 1127 definition of 'dilution' (the Act moved to a likelihood-of-dilution standard with blurring/tarnishment definitions in 1125(c)).
why: The Act removed the definitional text the Court used to confirm the actual-dilution requirement and replaced the standard with likelihood of dilution; the House report discusses Moseley's actual-dilution holding as the problem addressed.

label: override_express
decision: Georgia v. Ashcroft
title: Fannie Lou Hamer, Rosa Parks, and Coretta Scott King Voting Rights Act Reauthorization and Amendments Act of 2006
point: Held that retrogression is judged by the totality of circumstances, letting a state trade safe majority-minority districts for influence and coalition districts.
change: Added 1973c(b) and (d) making diminished ability to elect preferred candidates the test.
why: The amendment restores the ability-to-elect standard the decision displaced, and the findings and report name Georgia v. Ashcroft.

label: override_express
decision: Freightliner of Grand Rapids, Inc. v. United States
title: Safe, Accountable, Flexible, Efficient Transportation Equity Act: A Legacy for Users" or "SAFETEA-LU
point: Held that tractors are subject to the 4051 retail excise tax regardless of gross vehicle weight absent a will-not-equip certificate, so the light chassis cabs were taxable.
change: Added 4051(a)(4) excluding tractors with a gross vehicle weight of 19,500 pounds or less and gross combined weight of 33,000 pounds or less.
why: The new exclusion reverses the decision's regardless-of-weight rule for light tractors, and the conference report cites this decision as the holding being addressed.

decision: United States ex rel. Atkins v. McInteer
title: Fraud Enforcement and Recovery Act of 2009" or "FERA
point: Following Totten, held FCA 3729(a)(1) and conspiracy liability require presentment of a claim to a federal officer or employee, so claims submitted to the state Medicaid agency were not actionable.
change: FERA removed the 'to an officer or employee of the United States Government' presentment language and made liability turn on false claims, including requests to grantees.
why: The amendment eliminates the presentment requirement the court relied on, and the committee report cites this decision as an example of the Totten line it corrects.

label: override_express
decision: Harvey v. Veneman
title: Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2006
point: Held that 6510(a)(1) bars adding any synthetic ingredient in handling, invalidating rules allowing listed synthetics in processed organic foods.
change: Inserted 'not appearing on the National List' into 6510(a)(1).
why: The amendment permits National List synthetics, reversing the holding, and the same Act names Harvey v. Veneman.

label: override_express
decision: United States ex rel. Huangyan Import & Export Corp. v. Nature's Farm Products, Inc.
title: Fraud Enforcement and Recovery Act of 2009" or "FERA
point: Held that the FCA conspiracy provision, 3729(a)(3), reaches only conspiracies to get a false claim paid and not conspiracies to commit reverse false claims under (a)(7).
change: FERA rewrote the conspiracy provision to cover conspiracies to violate any of subparagraphs (A), (B), (D), (E), (F) or (G), including reverse false claims.
why: The new words would make the conspiracy claim viable, and the committee report cites this decision as the holding being corrected.

label: override_implicit
decision: Dunaway v. Ford Motor Co.
title: ADA Amendments Act of 2008
point: Held Dunaway was not 'regarded as' disabled because he lacked evidence Ford believed his knee condition substantially limited a major life activity, applying Sutton and Toyota.
change: Changed 12112(a) to bar discrimination 'on the basis of disability' and, in the same Act, redefined 'regarded as' so it no longer requires a perceived substantial limitation.
why: Under the ADAAA a perceived impairment suffices for a regarded-as claim, so the decision's reasoning no longer works; the Act rejected Sutton and Toyota, not this decision by name.

label: override_express
decision: United States ex rel. DRC, Inc. v. Custer Battles, LLC
title: Fraud Enforcement and Recovery Act of 2009" or "FERA
point: Held that requests for payment from Iraqi funds administered by the CPA were not FCA 'claims' unless the United States provided the money, rejecting the custodian theory.
change: FERA rewrote 3729(a), removing the requirement that the claim be presented to a U.S. officer, and redefined 'claim' to cover requests for money 'whether or not the United States has title' to it.
why: The new definition reverses the rule that government-administered non-U.S. funds fall outside the FCA, and the committee report names this litigation as wrongly decided.

label: override_express
decision: Ledbetter v. Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co.
title: Lilly Ledbetter Fair Pay Act of 2009
point: Held that a Title VII disparate-pay claim is timely under 2000e-5(e)(1) only as to pay decisions within the charge period, so the employee may reach back no further than the last pay decision before that period.
change: Added 2000e-5(e)(3): a compensation practice occurs each time discriminatory pay is paid, with back pay for up to two years.
why: The paycheck-accrual rule reverses the decision's timeliness rule, and the Act's findings name the Supreme Court decision affirming it in this same case.

label: override_express
decision: Hamdan v. Rumsfeld
title: Military Commissions Act of 2006
point: The Court held that 10 U.S.C. 821 (Art. 21) conditions the use of military commissions on compliance with the law of war, including Common Article 3, so the Guantanamo commission lacked power to proceed (and a plurality found conspiracy not triable by commission).
change: The Military Commissions Act added that 821 does not apply to military commissions established under new chapter 47A.
why: By making 821 inapplicable to the new commissions, Congress removed the statutory basis of Hamdan's holding, and the legislative record names Hamdan as what the Act responds to.

label: override_implicit
decision: Louis Vuitton Malletier v. Dooney & Bourke, Inc.
title: Trademark Dilution Revision Act of 2006
point: Affirmed denial of a preliminary injunction on the federal dilution claim because Vuitton showed no actual dilution under the 1127 definition as read in Moseley.
change: The TDRA struck the 1127 definition of dilution and replaced it with a likelihood-of-dilution standard for blurring and tarnishment.
why: Under the new words actual dilution is no longer required, so the ground on which the dilution claim failed is gone; Congress was responding to Moseley, not this decision.

label: override_express
decision: Santos v. United States
title: Fraud Enforcement and Recovery Act of 2009" or "FERA
point: Held 'proceeds' in the money-laundering statutes means net profits rather than gross receipts (following Scialabba), and vacated the convictions.
change: FERA made 1957's 'proceeds' take the 1956 definition, which FERA added to cover gross receipts.
why: Congress reversed the profits reading, and the report says it is correcting the Supreme Court's Santos decision, which affirmed this decision.

label: override_express
decision: Ledbetter v. Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co.
title: Lilly Ledbetter Fair Pay Act of 2009
point: Held that a Title VII pay-discrimination charge is untimely unless filed within 180 days of the discriminatory pay decision, not of later paychecks.
change: Added 2000e-5(e)(3) making each paycheck affected by a discriminatory compensation decision a new unlawful employment practice that restarts the charge period.
why: The Act names Ledbetter in its findings and directly reverses its timeliness rule.

label: override_implicit
decision: T.W.R., Inc. v. United States Secretary of Agriculture
title: American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009
point: Held that 2401e(a)(1)(C)'s net-income test requires comparing the producer's most recent year with the immediately preceding year, rejecting the Department's non-consecutive-year comparison, and remanded.
change: ARRA rewrote 2401e(a)(1), eliminating the net farm income comparison and substituting production, price, and county-price decline tests tied to the petition marketing year.
why: The net-income requirement the decision construed was removed, so its reasoning no longer applies; nothing shows Congress was responding to this case rather than overhauling the program.

label: override_express
decision: Allison Engine Co. v. United States ex rel. Sanders
title: Fraud Enforcement and Recovery Act of 2009" or "FERA
point: Held that 3729(a)(2) requires proof the defendant intended the false record to get a claim paid or approved by the Government, and (a)(3) requires an agreement to that end.
change: FERA rewrote (a)(2) to cover a false record or statement 'material to a false or fraudulent claim' and (a)(3) to cover conspiracy to commit any violation, dropping the 'to get ... paid or approved by the Government' language.
why: The new words remove the intent-to-get-Government-payment requirement the Court adopted, and the committee report expressly says it corrects Allison Engine.

label: override_express
decision: United States ex rel. DRC, Inc. v. Custer Battles, LLC
title: Fraud Enforcement and Recovery Act of 2009" or "FERA
point: Held that 3729(a)(1) requires presentment to U.S. officers or employees (finding the evidence sufficient here), that (a)(2) has no presentment requirement, and that claims on CPA-administered non-appropriated funds were qualifying claims.
change: FERA removed the presentment-to-an-officer language from (a)(1), made (a)(2) turn on materiality, and broadened 'claim' to cover funds the Government provides or administers.
why: The court's (a)(1) presentment rule is eliminated and the report expressly responds to the Custer Battles litigation (on Iraqi funds administered by the U.S.); Congress's funds change agrees with this panel's result, so the override is on the presentment point.

label: override_implicit
decision: United States v. Wright
title: Amy, Vicky, and Andy Child Pornography Victim Assistance Act of 2018
point: Following In re Amy, read 2259 as not limiting a child-pornography victim's losses to those proximately caused by the possessor, but vacated an unexplained $529,661 award.
change: The 2018 Act requires the court to find the victim's full losses and then order restitution reflecting the defendant's relative role in the causal process (minimum $3,000), with an aggregate cap.
why: The new text replaces the no-proximate-cause, full-losses approach the decision applied with a causation-based relative-role measure, but nothing in the packet shows Congress was responding to this decision.

label: override_express
decision: United States v. Nagarwala
title: Strengthening the Opposition to Female Genital Mutilation Act of 2020
point: Held that 18 U.S.C. 116(a) (FGM) exceeded Congress's Commerce Clause and Necessary and Proper powers.
change: Rewrote 116 to add interstate/foreign commerce and other jurisdictional elements and broaden the offence.
